To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found that vancomycin resistance is heterogeneous in MRSA isolates from a hospital in Italy.

the two strains of methicillin- resistant S. aureus (MRSA) isolated in our hospital had heterogeneous resistance to vancomycin, which may have been transferred between patients, and that the two strains were not resistant to linezolid.

1) the vancomycin resistance in S. aureus is heterogeneous, 2) vanA and vanB genes are not present in these isolates, 3) the vancomycins resistance is mediated by a new van gene, named vanH, 4) this new van gene is not related to the vanA and vanC genes, 5) the vanH gene is not present in the S. aureus ATCC 29213 strain, and 6
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the resistance to vancomycin in S. aureus.
the development of an effective method for the identification of the most relevant virulence factors of S. aureus, in particular of the methicillin-resistant strains.
the development of a novel method to detect the presence of methicillin-resistant staphylococcus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at least at the moment, there is no evidence that vancomycin resistance has emerged in MRSA strains in our hospital.
, in the absence of a vancomycin MIC of >2 mg/liter, a single clone of S. aureus with heterogeneous resistance to vancomycin is not a threat to the hospital.
the presence of vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus in Italy is still a very rare event, and the risk of the emergence of vancomycin-resistant S. aureus strains is very low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new class of compounds that have the potential to be used in the clinic for the treatment of MRSA infections.
we have demonstrated a novel mechanism for resistance to vancomycin in S. aureus.
the use of a single clone for the study of the vancomycin-resistant S. aureus strains is not sufficient to identify the presence of the heteroresistance phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the vancomycin-resistant S. aureus isolates were not only heterogeneous in their resistance to vancomycin, but they were also heterogeneous in their resistance genes and in their susceptibility to teicoplanin.

we can use the same methods to study the evolution of antibiotic resistance in bacteria, but in this case we are studying how bacteria evolve to become resistant to vancomycin, a drug that is used to treat MRSA infections.
we can’t just rely on a single test to determine the resistance profile of a bacterial strain.
